2607.15565.title: Ask Twice, Look Twice: Prompt Echoing Resolves the Question-First Paradox in Vision-Language Models
2607.15565.paper_summary: Where should the question go in a vision-language model (VLM) prompt: before the image or after it? Intuition says before: knowing what is asked should tell the model where to look. Yet across visual question answering benchmarks, question-first prompting consistently underperforms the image-first ordering recommended for frontier VLMs, a phenomenon we term the question-first paradox. We trace the paradox to a conflict between two stages of VLM computation. Logit-lens and attention probes show the intuition is half right: a question placed before the image genuinely steers perception, moving image patch representations toward question-relevant concepts. The failure lies downstream. Stranded behind hundreds of image tokens, the question is barely attended by the answer token, which instead commits to image-driven (often wrong) answers; a causal attention knockout confirms that the answer reads the question only when the question follows the image. The diagnosis yields a training-free fix: question echoing, restating the question on both sides of the image so that one copy steers perception while the other is read out at answer time. The same division of labor appears in a fifty-year-old finding on human ``adjunct questions'', where repeating a question before and after a passage aids comprehension more than either position alone. Echoing the image as well brings further gains, restoring the whole-image view a causal decoder otherwise loses. The paradox holds across five open VLMs, costing up to 17.5 group-accuracy points. Echoed prompts close it and surpass the best single-pass ordering on NaturalBench, POPE, Winoground, and open-ended VQAv2, by up to 19 Winoground group-accuracy points, with no training, fine-tuning, or architecture change. The paradox reveals a trade-off between steering perception and preserving question access; echoing resolves it through prompt design alone.
2607.15565.paper_summary_zh: 在視覺語言模型 (VLM) 提示中，問題應該放在圖像之前還是之後？直覺告訴我們應該放在之前：知道所詢問的內容應該能告訴模型該看哪裡。 然而，在視覺問題回答基準中，問題優先的提示始終表現不如推薦的圖像優先排序，這種現象我們稱之為問題優先悖論。 我們將這一悖論追溯到 VLM 計算的兩個階段之間的衝突。 Logit-lens 和注意力探測顯示，這一直覺是部分正確的：放在圖像之前的問題確實能引導感知，將圖像片段的表示推向與問題相關的概念。 失敗發生在下游。 在數百個圖像標記後，問題幾乎沒有被答案標記關注，答案標記反而承諾於圖像驅動的（通常是錯誤的）答案；因果注意力的淘汰證實，只有在問題跟隨圖像時，答案才會閱讀問題。 這一診斷得出了一個無需訓練的解決方案：問題回聲，即在圖像的兩側重述問題，使得一個副本引導感知，而另一個在回答時被讀出。 在人類的“附加問題”中，這種勞動分工也出現了，重複問題在段落前後有助於理解，效果超過單獨的任一位置。 回聲圖像也帶來進一步的收益，恢復了因果解碼器本來會失去的整體圖像視圖。 這一悖論在五個開放的 VLM 中持續存在，最多損失 17.5 個群體準確率點。 回聲提示縮小了這一差距，並在 NaturalBench、POPE、Winoground 和開放式 VQAv2 上超越了最佳的單次通過排序，最多提升 19 個 Winoground 群體準確率點，且無需訓練、微調或架構變更。 這一悖論揭示了引導感知與保留問題訪問之間的權衡；回聲通過提示設計單獨解決了這一問題。
